sections.h2: Where do I search property records in Pinellas County?
sections.html:
Start with the Official Records search run by the Pinellas County Clerk of the Circuit Court and Comptroller at mypinellasclerk.gov. The clerk's records page groups land records, deeds, mortgages, liens, judgments and plats in one place, separate from court case records.

The clerk's records liaison is at 315 Court Street, Room 400, Clearwater, FL 33756, with a phone line at (727) 464-3341. The Customer Information Center number printed on the fee schedule is (727) 464-7000. If a document is not free online, the clerk's copy request center gives a quote.

Ownership, parcel and value data live elsewhere, at the property appraiser. The appraiser's site at pcpao.gov offers quick, map and advanced search for real property and tangible personal property. Use both: the clerk shows what was recorded, and the appraiser shows how the parcel is valued and who is on the tax roll.

sections.h2: What does Pinellas County look like for a house sale?
sections.html:
Pinellas is a peninsula 38 miles long and 15 miles wide at its widest point, with 280 square miles and 588 miles of coastline. The county's own fast facts page calls it the most densely populated county in Florida, at 3,425 people per square mile, and the second smallest by land area.

It became the state's 48th county on January 1, 1912, when voters chose to separate from Hillsborough County. Clearwater is the county seat, St. Petersburg is the largest of 24 municipalities, and Tarpon Springs was the first city incorporated, in 1887. The 2020 Census counted 959,107 residents, which ranks seventh in the state.

The county lists tourism, financial services, life science, manufacturing, defense, aviation and information technology as key sectors. The practical point for sellers is that the county contains 24 cities with separate codes. A parcel may be inside a city or in unincorporated land, and the deed and records work is the same either way because one clerk records for the whole county.

sections.h2: How many parcels and what kinds of property are in the county?
sections.html:
The property appraiser's home page lists 437,624 real property parcels, of which 408,947 are residential. That mix includes 241,442 single family units, 103,445 condo units, 22,112 townhome or PUD units, 44,323 manufactured home units and 101,180 multifamily rental units.

The same list shows 23,010 commercial parcels and 57,476 tangible personal property accounts. If your home is a condo or a manufactured home unit, ask the clerk which recorded documents apply to it.

sections.h2: Which fees apply when a Pinellas deed is recorded?
sections.html:
The fee comes from Florida law, plus the documentary stamp tax on the deed itself. The clerk's fee schedule is a PDF at mypinellasclerk.gov/Home/Fee-Schedule, and it says the charges are set by statute, county ordinance and administrative order.

Section 28.24(13) of the Florida Statutes sets the recording charge at $5.00 on page one and $4.00 on every later page of an instrument up to 14 by 8.5 inches. It also adds $1.00 for each name beyond four, a Public Records Modernization Trust Fund charge of $1.00 on the first page and $0.50 on each additional page, and a $4 per page technology charge.

Deed stamp tax is 70 cents on each $100 of consideration in Pinellas, as in all counties other than Miami-Dade. Consideration includes any mortgage or encumbrance on the property, whether or not the buyer assumes it. Every party to the deed is liable, whichever party agrees to pay. Ask the title company for the final recording total before closing.

  • Taxable deeds include warranty, special warranty, quit claim, trustee's and life estate deeds, a deed in lieu of foreclosure and a contract for deed.
  • A personal representative's deed under a probated will is listed as not taxable.
  • A spousal homestead deed whose only consideration is a mortgage, and a divorce deed for the marital home, are exempt.

sections.h2: What does a Florida deed need before the clerk can record it?
sections.html:
A conveyance of land must be in writing and signed in the presence of two subscribing witnesses under section 689.01 of the Florida Statutes. No seal is required, and the witnessing may be done by audio-video technology.

Other charges can sit on the same closing statement. Mortgages and notes carry documentary stamp tax of 35 cents per $100 of the amount secured, and the tax on a note is capped at $2,450 with no cap on mortgages. The clerk's schedule under section 28.24 also lists a $60.00 tax deed application processing charge and plat fees of $30.00 for the first page and $15.00 for each additional page.

Recording matters because an unrecorded conveyance can lose out to a later buyer. Ask your title company to record the deed on the day of closing and to send you the recorded copy.

sections.h2: What should I check in the records before selling a house in Pinellas County?
sections.html:
Pull the chain of title and look for anything recorded against the property that a buyer's title company will find. Typical finds are an old mortgage never released, a contractor's lien, or a judgment recorded under an owner's name.

  • Search the owner's name and the legal description, not only the street address.
  • Look for recorded mortgages without a matching satisfaction.
  • Look for liens, judgments and code enforcement filings.
  • Confirm the deed in your name was recorded and names every owner correctly.

A lady bird deed, which keeps full powers with the life tenants, was addressed by the Florida Department of Revenue in a 2020 advisement that said it does not transfer a present beneficial interest and is not subject to documentary stamp tax on the facts presented. That is guidance on one set of facts, so a title attorney should review yours.

Any transfer of title is a change of ownership for Save Our Homes unless an exception applies, such as a transfer between spouses. A quitclaim to a relative can therefore reset the assessment to market value the next January 1.

faqs.q: Who is the recorder for Pinellas County?
faqs.a: The Clerk of the Circuit Court and Comptroller. The clerk's office keeps deeds, mortgages, liens, judgments and plats, and its records page links to the search.

faqs.q: Can I search Pinellas County deeds online?
faqs.a: Yes, through the Official Records search that the clerk's View Records page links to. Items not free online can be requested through the clerk's copy request center, which gives a cost quote.

faqs.q: How much is the documentary stamp tax on a Pinellas County deed?
faqs.a: It is 70 cents per $100 of consideration. All counties except Miami-Dade use that rate, and the clerk takes it at recording.

faqs.q: What is the statutory recording fee in Pinellas County?
faqs.a: Section 28.24(13) sets $5.00 on page one and $4.00 for each later page, before the trust fund and technology charges. Check the clerk's PDF fee schedule for the current total.

faqs.q: Where do I find parcel and value information for Pinellas County?
faqs.a: Use the property appraiser at pcpao.gov, which offers address, owner, parcel ID and map search. The office lists four service locations and a main phone line of (727) 464-3207.
